source_span: There's very little in the Muse offering to suggest it disrupts the unit economics of the banking system, and the bigger issue with AI right now... is that it's completely untrustworthy.
source_chain: Banks/WM sold off hard with consensus mega-cap names (C, MS, GS, USB) dominating selling volume while regionals/boutiques (LAZ, JEF) outperformed, therefore this pattern reads as a positioning unwind / systematic de-risking rather than a fundamental repricing, because Muse doesn't actually disrupt bank unit economics and Meta's own trust problem undercuts the disintermediation thesis, therefore O'Dwyer wants to fade the move (buy banks), sized patiently, favoring MS/PNC/FITB. Invalidation: if selling instead concentrated in non-consensus/regional names (evidence of genuine fundamental repricing rather than positioning unwind), the fade thesis breaks.
pulse_chain: XLF and the Consumer Inertia basket sold off on the agentic-disruption narrative, therefore two desks read the same selling differently: JPMorgan's O'Dwyer argues fundamentals don't support it (Muse doesn't disrupt bank unit economics), calls it a positioning-unwind signature not a re-rating (citing consensus names dominating volume vs. regional outperformance), and wants to fade it, sized patiently, favoring MS/PNC/Fifth Third; Goldman does not argue fundamentals back, instead calling it an uncertainty discount and a complete buyers' strike, counseling patience over defense per past AI selloffs. Therefore resolution comes from upcoming product catalysts (Meta Connect, OpenAI Dev Day, Micron earnings), not valuation.
why: The pulse reproduces O'Dwyer's exact reasoning chain (no unit-economics disruption → positioning-unwind not re-rating, evidenced by consensus-name selling vs. regional outperformance → fade, sized patiently, favoring MS/PNC/FITB) and correctly contrasts it with Goldman's distinct non-fundamental uncertainty-discount/buyers'-strike/patience framing, with no reversed step, misattribution, or invented mechanism.
